name: AKU Achieves Full AAALAC International Accreditation

content.text: The accreditation follows an extensive review process that began in 2021, including multiple rounds of evaluation followed by program improvements addressing the findings. The AAALAC International Council recently confirmed that all previous review findings have been addressed in accordance with global benchmarks commended the University for its thoughtful improvements and approved its accreditation with AAALAC International.

"AAALAC International is the only accreditation agency of its kind that evaluates animal research programs around the world," said Dr Tashfeen, Head of the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee. "It's not just a title; it's a global mark of credibility. Even the World Health Organization and National Institutes of Health, U.S. look for this accreditation when considering research partnerships."

For AKU, the journey toward accreditation began long before the review process. "When I was appointed to lead the animal program at the University in 2012, a process for review and approval of animal care and use was in-place and an animal facility was functional, but these were not fully aligned with the current best international standards," shared Dr Tashfeen. "Over the years, we worked hard to bring operational practices in line with our institutional mission and global expectations. Today, the quality of our animal care and use program truly reflects AKU's vision."

When asked how the University ensures animals are treated with care and respect, he emphasized a culture of ethical responsibility. "We provide detailed guidelines to everyone involved, scientists, veterinarians, and staff, ensuring that all handling of animals is humane and adheres to strict safety protocols. We always explore alternatives before involving animals in research." Students and faculty in biomedical and life sciences also benefit from this structured, ethical approach. "The health and safety of our researchers, particularly students, is a priority," said Dr Tashfeen. "Protocols are in place to protect them from allergies and harmful animal exposure. Students also gain hands-on learning opportunities in a way that prepares them for real-world biomedical research, without compromising on ethics."

Now fully accredited for its mouse and rat research facility, the University's responsibilities continue. "AAALAC International has defined conditions that we must continue to fulfill, and we are committed to ongoing improvement," he noted. "We regularly hold workshops and lectures, collaborating with other educational institutions from across Pakistan. We're also in conversation with the government, because currently, there are no national laws on the ethical use of animals in research, and that needs to change."

In a heartfelt message to students and young researchers, Dr Tashfeen said, "Whenever you are dealing with animals, remember they can feel pain and distress. It's our moral duty to minimize their suffering. Always consider alternatives first, and if animals must be used, do so with the utmost care and respect."

This achievement would not have been possible without the visionary leadership and relentless support by the Institutional Official for the Animal Programme Dr. Syed Ather Enam, and Director Laboratories Dr. Azhar Hussain, and the tireless dedication of members of the Ethics Committee for Animal Care and Use, Institutional Biosafety Committee, lab management, technical and admin staff, and numerous colleagues in Design, Project Management, Facilities Management, Family Medicine, Security, Purchase and other departments behind the scenes. Dr Tashfeen expressed his special gratitude to former Dean Dr. Adil Haider, Vice Provosts Dr. Fauziah Rabbani and Dr. Anjum Halai, Provost Dr. Carl Amrhein, Dean Research and Graduate Studies Dr. Elnasir Lalani, and Associate Dean Research Dr. Anwar Ali Siddiqui.

content.author: Faiza Hakim Shah
content.description: The Aga Khan University Medical College has been granted full accreditation by AAALAC International, an internationally respected recognition that highlights AKU's commitment to the highest standards of animal care and ethical research practices.
